checked: Royce p. 856-857: April 9, 1872 executive order setting apart the Colville reservation east of the Columbia (boundaries match the promise); remark 'Restored to public domain by Executive order of July 2, 1872' and the 1881 Spokane reserve; area 533, Washington 1. Matches.

ICC Docket 181 finding 5 (OSU id 441): the April 9 order, its revocation on July 2, 1872, and the petition excluding lands inside the July 2 reservation. Finding 42: white squatters, most of them east of the Columbia within the April 9 reservation, bore on moving the reservation west; non-reservation lands taken without compensation as of July 2, 1872.

Under Jordan's EO rule the July 2 revocation alone is not a breach; this record is broken on the Commission's finding about the Colville and Lakes tracts, which lie inside this tract (1959 opinion, OSU id 191). So it rests on a finding about its own land.
Awards: Colville $111,000 and Lake $125,000 (OSU id 248); Colville net $104,600 after offsets (OSU id 568).
